USGS 04010510 is a discharge and stage gauge on the Grand Portage River at Grand Portage. DNR Lake Superior trail materials identify the Grand Portage River beach/corridor, and NPS documents canoe access and portage context, so it is route-capable; however, no existing scored route or complete endpoint/threshold package uses this provider key.
blockers: No existing scored route explicitly uses USGS provider key 04010510.
Limited-access tribal/reservation context requires a dedicated endpoint, rights, safety, and threshold package.

reviews.decisionReason: At least one scored route uses this gauge directly.

USGS 04015438 is live on the upper St. Louis River near Skibo, and DNR identifies the Skibo Mills / Highway 100 corridor as paddle-relevant but boulder-bed and low-water sensitive. The current same-run reading was only 0.75 cfs / 16.89 ft, and no route-specific USGS 04015438 paddling threshold, selected endpoint pair, camping/no-camping package, safety package, coordinate package, image decision, or geometry cleared for a new scored route.
blockers: Same-run USGS telemetry showed only 0.75 cfs at Skibo, far below any practical St. Louis paddling package reviewed in this run.
DNR warns the Skibo Mills to Highway 100 upper St. Louis boulder-bed corridor may be impassable at medium to low water levels.
No public manager/source package tied USGS 04015438 to a selected endpoint pair, numeric threshold model, legal camping/no-camping terms, endpoint coordinates, image decision, and route geometry.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 04021520 is Stoney Brook at Pine Drive near Brookston, a tributary gauge rather than a selected St. Louis River water-trail reach. Same-run discharge was the USGS missing-value sentinel with a backwater qualifier, and no official point-to-point paddling corridor, thresholds, public endpoint pair, camping/no-camping terms, safety package, coordinates, image, or geometry surfaced for Stoney Brook.
blockers: The gauge is on Stoney Brook, not on an official selected St. Louis River day-route reach.
Same-run USGS discharge was -999999 with a backwater qualifier, so discharge is not usable for route scoring.
No public route package exists for a Stoney Brook point-to-point paddle with endpoints, thresholds, camping, safety, coordinates, image, and geometry.

reviews.decisionReason: The gauge is explicitly recorded as stale, inapplicable, or unavailable to the product.

USGS 04024000 is the provider-equivalent Scanlon gauge for MN DNR site 239. It has extensive live stream telemetry and the official DNR St. Louis map places the gauge beside Scanlon access, but the same Scanlon-to-Thomson reach remains expert whitewater with no-portage dams and no product-ready route-specific threshold and safety package.
blockers: Provider-equivalent MN DNR site 239 is blocked for the same Scanlon expert-whitewater/no-portage corridor.
No scored route cleared a route-specific numeric paddling threshold, endpoint, skill/routeType, camping, safety, image, or geometry package for this station.
Any future use requires explicit expert-whitewater handling and manager-backed dam/portage guidance.
evidence: https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/USGS-04024000/ identifies St. Louis River at Scanlon, MN with continuous, daily, and field data and coordinates 46.703511, -92.418378.
https://files.dnr.state.mn.us/maps/canoe_routes/stlouis3.pdf places Scanlon carry-in access and the river-level gauge beside Scanlon Dam and Thomson Reservoir, with Class IV-V hazards and no portage.

https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/state-water-trails/st-louis-river/segments-maps.html describes the same corridor as expert-only whitewater in many sections and warns of multiple dams and Class I-VI rapids.

reviews.decisionReason: Wisconsin DNR documents canoe access to the Nemadji River Floodplain Forest near South Superior, while Superior reports paddling access; the active gauge is route-relevant but no product package resolves endpoints, turbidity/impairment caveats, and Lake Superior confluence safety.
blockers: no product route package currently covers the South Superior gauge reach
turbidity impairment and Lake Superior confluence hazards require explicit safety treatment

reviews.decisionReason: At least one scored route uses this gauge directly.

USGS 04026160 monitors the Siskiwit River at Cornucopia. Bayfield County and Lake Superior water-trail sources document public shoreline access at Siskiwit Bay, Cornucopia paddling services, and the river mouth/estuary context. A route-capable corridor exists, but the gauge is river-mouth/coastal and no station-specific thresholds, river endpoint pair, Lake Superior hazard package, camping terms, coordinates, imagery, or geometry has been validated.
blockers: River-mouth/coastal hazard and endpoint package need validation
Station-specific thresholds need authoritative confirmation
Camping, coordinates, imagery, and geometry package not validated

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 040263205 is an active Whittlesey Creek station near Ashland with discharge and stage telemetry. Federal and regional sources document canoe/kayak use in the Whittlesey Creek estuary and Lake Superior coastal complex, but no distinct upstream point-to-point route from the Cherryville Road station has a validated public endpoint, safety, camping/no-camping, coordinate, image, geometry, and station-specific threshold package. The estuary evidence is not treated as direct route coverage for the upstream gauge without that package.
blockers: No validated upstream put-in/take-out pair tied to the Cherryville Road station.
Estuary and coastal paddling evidence does not establish direct station-corridor thresholds.
Complete safety, camping/no-camping, coordinate, image, and geometry package is not yet validated.

reviews.decisionReason: The Beartrap Creek station appears in historical USGS records, but current route-capable evidence is absent: no current PaddleToday-ready point-to-point corridor, public endpoints, threshold, access/camping, safety, coordinate, image, or geometry package was found. Treat the historical gauge as unsupported until current station and route evidence is refreshed.

The public USGS page also identifies the station as discontinued for funding reasons, so a route promotion requires refreshed current-station and access evidence.

USGS 05030500 is the Otter Tail River near Elizabeth and is provider-equivalent to the covered MN DNR Elizabeth gauge used by the existing Otter Tail scored routes. The existing route packages already carry official DNR bands, endpoints, camping, hazards, and geometry; a second USGS record would duplicate the same corridor without adding route value.
blockers: Provider-equivalent to covered MN DNR Elizabeth gauge 159.
Existing Otter Tail routes already contain the endpoint, camping, safety, geometry, and threshold package.
Cross-provider duplication adds no distinct scored-route value.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05046000 is the provider counterpart to MN DNR gauge 158 below Orwell Dam. The official Otter Tail Map 2 and USACE Orwell Lake materials establish the same dam/reservoir hazard and access context, while the existing Otter Tail route package uses the DNR Elizabeth gauge and DNR-recommended reaches. A second provider record would not add a distinct endpoint, threshold, camping, or safety package.
blockers: Provider-equivalent to blocked MN DNR gauge 158.
Orwell Dam/reservoir requires the same unresolved portage and access treatment.
Duplicate provider record adds no distinct route-quality value.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05049000 is the Mustinka River above Wheaton. The station has live and historical stream data, but the current Minnesota DNR water-trail and public-access materials do not establish a distinct, route-ready Mustinka endpoint pair, camping package, or paddling threshold interpretation. Without that evidence, adding a scored route would be speculative even though the gauge is technically route-capable.
blockers: No current DNR water-trail segment or named public endpoint pair established.
No source-backed paddling threshold interpretation for this station.
Camping, safety, and river-line evidence would require a separate discovery effort.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05049710 is a stage-only station at the Lake Traverse Reservation Dam. Official Minnesota paddling material places the supported Otter Tail State Water Trail downstream near Wheaton, while this station is a reservoir/dam-control location with no current point-to-point PaddleToday route corridor or river-specific threshold package.
blockers: No official state-water-trail or recommended river section uses the Reservation Dam gauge as a route gauge.
Telemetry is gage height only and describes reservoir/dam control rather than a paddle-specific river reach.
No named public point-to-point route package, thresholds, camping, safety, or geometry was found for this station.

evidence.label: USGS station 05049710

evidence.label: Minnesota DNR Otter Tail State Water Trail Map 1
evidence.note: Official paddling route begins at Wannigan Road and continues downstream; it does not establish a Reservation Dam route.

evidence.label: U.S. Army Corps Lake Traverse recreation and dam information
evidence.note: Federal source describes Reservation Dam as reservoir water-control infrastructure, not a river route package.

reviews.decisionReason: Gauge is known from route or audit evidence but has not been durably adjudicated.

USGS confirms a live Bois de Sioux gauge near Doran, but current official Minnesota DNR water-trail materials document the Otter Tail joining the Bois de Sioux at Breckenridge rather than a supported Bois de Sioux route segment. No PaddleToday-ready public endpoint pair, threshold, camping/permit, safety, and coordinate package was found for the gauge reach.
blockers: No official DNR Bois de Sioux paddling segment or complete endpoint pair found for the Doran gauge reach.
Historical/secondary paddling references are insufficient to establish a current safe, thresholded PaddleToday route package.

evidence.note: USGS monitoring location identifies Bois de Sioux River near Doran and provides current discharge and gage-height telemetry.
Minnesota DNR documents the Otter Tail State Water Trail and its confluence with the Bois de Sioux at Breckenridge, but does not establish a Bois de Sioux segment for this gauge.
USGS annual report places the gauge at the County Highway 6 bridge and notes regulated flow; this is gauge context, not a route package.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05051500 is product-live on the Red River of the North at Wahpeton and overlaps the official Kidder Recreation Area-to-Brushvale Bridge water-trail corridor, but the existing scored same-reach route uses MN DNR gauge 318 with official interpreted stage bands. Under provider:siteId coverage identity, the USGS key is not covered, and a duplicate USGS-gauged card would lack source-backed paddling thresholds tied to 05051500.
blockers: provider-equivalent same-reach scored route already exists as red-river-kidder-brushvale using mn_dnr:318
no accepted numeric paddling threshold model tied to USGS 05051500
duplicate route would add no new access, camping, safety, coordinate, image, or geometry value

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 0505152130 is product-live on the Red River of the North at Enloe in the broad MN DNR Red River water-trail corridor, but no Enloe-specific scored route package cleared. Official sources support the broader river and warn to check water levels, low water, snags, dams, flooding, and state-border rules, but they do not provide selected Enloe endpoints, station-specific thresholds, camping terms, safety handling, coordinate package, image decision, or geometry.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05489000 is a live Cedar Creek discharge and stage station with a 374-square-mile drainage area. blockers: Official Cedar Creek paddling geometry is not yet tied to a station-specific endpoint pair.

Camping, hazard, image, coordinate, and route-order evidence remains incomplete.
